title: Inspect the Payment History
scenario: It is 10:40 AM. Before paying INV-58831, the desk asks a blunt question: have we paid this already? The Payment History is the record of every invoice already paid. Inspect it - and learn how yesterday's run becomes today's guardrail against paying the same bill twice.
input: Paid invoices as of the day-0 run: INV-58790 | V-1042 Northwind Fasteners | 980.00 | day-0. (Plus other vendors' prior payments.) Identity key for a paid invoice = vendor id + invoice number + invoice total. INV-58831 does not appear here.
instructions: Read the Payment History as the record of what has already been paid.
Answer the four questions against the history and the workflow map.
Validate to mint the payment-history source profile.

questions.prompt: What is the Payment History used to prevent?
questions.explain: Duplicate payment is one of the most common and expensive AP errors. The history is the record the duplicate check compares each new invoice against.

questions.prompt: What is the identity key that decides whether two invoices are the same?

options.text: Vendor id + invoice number + invoice total

questions.explain: A single field is too weak - vendors reuse numbers and totals recur. Combining vendor, invoice number, and total gives a reliable identity for a specific bill.

questions.prompt: INV-58831 is not in the history. What does that tell the duplicate check?

options.text: It has not been paid before - not a duplicate
It must be paid immediately, skipping the match
It is invalid and should be rejected

questions.explain: Absence from the paid history means this exact bill has not gone out before. It still must pass the three-way match - the duplicate check only rules out double payment.

questions.prompt: Where does the Payment History get updated from each day?

options.text: The Payment Archive, when the run is archived

questions.explain: Follow the map's temporal loop: when today's run is archived, it seeds the history, so tomorrow's duplicate check sees today's payments. Yesterday's output is today's guardrail.

intro.heading: Before you match: guard against double payment

sections.title: Yesterday guards today
sections.body: The Payment History is every invoice already paid. Checking a new invoice against it is how the desk avoids the classic, costly mistake of paying the same bill twice.

sections.title: Identity needs three fields
sections.body: Vendor id, invoice number, and total together identify a specific bill. Any one alone is too weak - numbers get reused and totals recur across unrelated invoices.

sections.title: Absence means clear
sections.body: INV-58831 is not in the history, so it has not been paid before. That clears the duplicate check - but it still has to pass the three-way match on its own merits.

sections.title: The temporal loop
sections.body: When today's run is archived it seeds the history. That is the loop on the map: an output that becomes tomorrow's reference. You inspect it today; you will close the loop at the archive step.

takeaway.heading: Payment History inspected
points: You answered the four questions: what it prevents, the identity key, what absence means, and how it is seeded.
The history is the baseline the duplicate check reads to stop the desk paying a bill twice.
Identity is vendor id + invoice number + total together - no single field is strong enough.
The history is seeded by the Payment Archive, so yesterday's run becomes today's guardrail - the map's temporal loop.
The workflow can now tell whether an invoice has already been paid before it pays again.
